StepRecord.description: A sanitized summary of one completed step. Raw values, secrets, value_ref contents, and full URLs must NEVER appear here — only structural metadata.

action.description: The action type that was executed (click, type, scroll, etc.).

element_id.description: The element that was targeted, if any. Null for non-element actions.

element_label.description: The sanitized label of the targeted element, as it appeared in the context. Redaction tokens (e.g. [EMAIL_01]) are safe to include here since they carry no real value. Raw field values must never appear here.

outcome.description: Verification outcome from the extension's PVM layer.

title: SanitizedContext
description: The only payload shape allowed to leave the browser. Built by the extension's Privacy Firewall after redaction (extension/src/privacy/redact.ts), validated again server-side (server/app/validators/context_validator.py) before any reasoning happens.

task.description: What the user actually asked for, in their own words, e.g. 'log in' or 'pick the cheaper flight'. Typed by the user in the extension popup — the agent does nothing without one. This is user-authored text, not page content, so it is not subject to redaction; the user is deliberately telling the model what they want.

page.description: Semantic page role, e.g. 'login', 'checkout' — not the raw URL path.

url_origin.description: Origin only (scheme + host). Full URLs with query params may leak PII and must never be sent.

route_hint.description: Optional. The CURRENT page's pathname only, e.g. '/search' or '/product/123' — never a full URL. Query strings, hash fragments, and credentials must already be stripped before this is built (extension/src/privacy/sanitizedContext.ts derives it straight from location.pathname, which excludes all three by construction). This is structural navigation context only: it is NOT the semantic page type ('checkout', 'login') that the `page` field's own description above calls for — nothing may infer a page's meaning from this value, client or server side. Optional and not in the top-level `required` list for backward compatibility with clients built before this field existed; absent means the route is unknown, never '/' by default.

disabled.description: True when the control is unavailable for interaction. The client derives this from the native `disabled` property, `aria-disabled`, and `fieldset[disabled]` inheritance (extension/src/perception/domCapture.ts). Optional: absent means 'not known to be disabled', which the server treats as false. This is factual UI state only — it carries no instruction about what the model should do with it.

value_state.description: Optional. WHETHER an editable control currently holds content — never WHAT it holds. A closed three-token enum by design: because no other string validates, a raw field value (a password, a query, any PII) can never travel in this field even if a client tried to put one here. 'empty' = editable and currently blank; 'nonempty' = currently holds content, contents deliberately not disclosed; 'redacted' = holds content the client classified as sensitive (a password/token-labelled field), likewise not disclosed — 'redacted' and 'nonempty' differ only in the client's sensitivity classification, and neither reveals content. Absent means the client does not report field state, which the server treats as unknown (NOT as empty) — the same 'absence is not a negative claim' convention `disabled` uses above. Reflects the CURRENT capture for this request, not a replay of past actions.

fields.description: Redacted field map only, e.g. { "email": "[EMAIL_01]" }. Every value here must be a redaction token, never a raw value — the server rejects anything that doesn't look like one.

history.description: Optional. Sanitized records of steps completed in this task so far. Absent or empty when this is the first step.
